title: The long-term Distribution Reward design has Executors pay recipients from their own Buffer and be reimbursed at settlement
content:
A.2.2.9.1.2.1.3.3.1 describes today's arrangement: Operational GovOps calculates the Distribution Reward and it is "paid from the Demand Side Buffer within seven (7) days of the end of every month" — a Sky-controlled account (A.2.2.4.3).

A.2.2.9.1.2.1.3.3.2 describes the destination and names the reason: Operational GovOps calculates the reward, "then pays the Distribution Reward recipient **from its Buffer**. Later Sky Core reimburses the Operational Agent Buffer for the amount paid as part of the Settlement Cycle. This minimizes the role of Sky Core in Distribution Reward payments and emphasizes the primary role of the Operational Executor Agent, acting through Operational GovOps, in implementing the Sky Primitives."

The change is not merely who signs the transaction. In the long-term model the Executor **fronts working capital** and carries reimbursement risk against Sky Core until the Settlement Cycle clears. That is a real balance-sheet requirement, and it makes Executor Agents financial intermediaries rather than purely operational ones — consistent with the Executor Accord's framing of Executors as providing "automated operational insurance" (A.2.2.6.1).

The stated benefit is architectural rather than economic: Sky Core recedes from the payment path, so recipients interact with the Executor that serves their Prime Agent, and Sky Core's role narrows to periodic net settlement. Payment volume can then scale with the number of Executors instead of through one central buffer.

The cost is that a Primitive's day-to-day reliability comes to depend on each Executor's liquidity, and Sky Core's obligation to reimburse becomes a recurring credit relationship rather than a direct disbursement.
description: Payment moves off Sky Core's balance sheet: Operational GovOps fronts each month's rewards and recovers them in the Settlement Cycle, making Executors the operational face of the Primitives.
